_comment: FusedSensorNet as two independent conv branches plus the LSTM tail -- the same shape flow_c's fused_split ships, now derived rather than transcribed: branch-mode slicing gives tiles 0 and 1 depends_on: [] and the tail the non-contiguous range [[8,9],[14,90]] (the vision Flatten+FC interleaves with the depth branch in topological order). Honest caveat, measured: in ISOLATION this split does not pay for its concurrency. The branches are 0.150 ms (vision) and 0.048 ms (depth) on CPU int8, less than the 0.367 ms DSP / 0.540 ms HTA dispatch that overlapping them would cost, so the best isolated assignment runs both on the CPU lane back to back: 0.548 ms makespan, against 0.452 ms for the contiguous fused_k3_convs slice set which folds the vision FC in with the depth convs. The split is still the right manifest for a shared schedule, because those CPU cells are the ones flow_c measures at ~5.6x in situ, and both branches here compose on HTA (0.607 / 0.540 ms) where the contiguous variant's second tile does not.

_provenance.statistic: median of per-sweep median_us, performance governor, CPU cells unmasked
_provenance.op_index_space: flow_c IR, taken from flow_c/bindings/fused_split.json, which already declares exactly this tile structure (two conv branches + LSTM tail) in IR space. The branch-mode ONNX partition derived here reproduces that structure independently -- tiles 0 and 1 come out with depends_on: [] and the tail with the non-contiguous ONNX range [[8,9],[14,90]] -- so the IR ranges are adopted rather than re-derived; the flow_c IR cached in gen/ir/fused_full carries dependency edges inconsistent with that manifest's indexing and was not trusted. _ops_onnx_nodes records the ONNX node ranges the artifacts were sliced from.
